subject: astronomy
title: Reading Spectra: Doppler and Composition
welcome_lead: Spectra tell you what a star is, how fast it is moving and how hot it is.
meta_desc: A-Level Astronomy: Doppler shifts, chemical composition and spectral analysis.
final_note: Almost everything we know about stars comes from their light.

concepts.def: Wavelength change due to relative motion.
Continuous spectrum with dark lines from cool gas.
Bright lines from hot gas at specific wavelengths.
Three rules describing continuous, emission and absorption spectra.

walkthroughs.body_html: If a star moves toward us, lines shift blue; away, red. Δλ/λ = v/c for non-relativistic speeds. Radial velocities of stars are measured this way to milli-pixel precision.
Each element has a fingerprint of lines. Identifying lines in a star reveals its composition. Line strength depends on temperature, so the lines also confirm spectral type.

1. A hot dense source emits a continuous spectrum. 2. A hot diffuse gas emits an emission spectrum. 3. A cool gas in front of a hot source produces an absorption spectrum — this is what we see from a star's photosphere.
